column1: # E35.8 — ZAP rule overrides for subenai.sk.
# E43 — calibration pass: explicit WARN→FAIL promotion plan per rule.
# Format (tab-separated):
#   <Rule ID>
# Default threshold for unlisted rules is WARN (set in workflow YAML).
# Bump a rule to FAIL once we've confirmed the finding type is real
# AND triaged out of the codebase. Bump to IGNORE only with a written
# justification (cite a follow-up epic or a documented accepted risk).
# Reference: https://www.zaproxy.org/docs/alerts/ — every rule ID
# below has a doc page at /docs/alerts/<ID>/.
# Calibration policy (E43, 2026-05-20):
#   1. Every WARN-graded rule below carries an explicit promotion
#      criterion: "promote to FAIL after N consecutive green baseline
#      runs". The Mon 04:00 UTC schedule produces one run/week, so
#      "N=4" means roughly one month.
#   2. Before promoting a rule, verify on the latest workflow run that
#      WARN-NEW=0 for that rule across the four runs. If the rule has
#      fired even once, reset the counter and document why.
#   3. IGNORE entries are forever-decisions. Adding a new IGNORE row
#      requires a write-up here AND a CHANGELOG entry — we don't want
#      ZAP coverage silently shrinking over time.
#   4. Promotion changes ship in a separate PR titled
#      `chore(security): promote ZAP rule <ID> WARN→FAIL`, NEVER
#      bundled with a feature PR.
#   Static marketing pages legitimately ship with Cache-Control headers
#   from Cloudflare. Not a vuln; just informational.

column3: Static legal/marketing pages are intentionally cacheable.

column1: #   We ship source maps in production for debuggability. Comments in
#   the bundle are React/Vite-generated, not secret leaks.

column3: Bundled React/Vite comments — no secret leakage.

column1: #   GA + Stripe responses include timestamps; not actionable.
#   Promotion plan: candidate for IGNORE — these are third-party
#   responses we don't control. Keep WARN one more month, then move
#   to IGNORE with a CHANGELOG note. Promoting to FAIL is not viable
#   because the source is external.
#   We DO set Permissions-Policy in `_headers`. If this flags, it means
#   ZAP saw a route that bypassed the header — investigate.
#   Promotion plan: PROMOTE TO FAIL after 4 consecutive green baseline
#   runs (target: 2026-06-15+). Coverage is already locked by
#   tests/security/headers-contract.ts so prod drift is the only way
#   this can fire — exactly what a FAIL signal should catch.

column3: Promote→FAIL once 4 green baselines confirm prod parity.

column2: Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set

column1: #   Same — we set CSP. A finding here means a route is leaking around
#   `_headers` (e.g. a route returned by an API endpoint without the
#   CF Pages header injection).
#   Promotion plan: PROMOTE TO FAIL together with 10063 — same
#   guarantee (file-locked) and same risk profile (drift only).

column3: Promote→FAIL with 10063 once 4 green baselines pass.

column1: #   We don't have form-based auth. Magic-link flow is rate-limited +
#   uses Turnstile. Stripe Checkout has its own CSRF cookie (`m`).
#   Flip to IGNORE if the only forms ZAP finds are the magic-link form.
#   Promotion plan: NEVER FAIL — ZAP's anti-CSRF detector is heuristic
#   and trips on any form, including search inputs. Move to IGNORE
#   once we've audited the next baseline report and confirmed every
#   flagged form is one of: magic-link (Turnstile-gated), Stripe
#   Checkout (CSRF=`m` cookie), Composer admin forms (admin role).

column3: Heuristic; audit one more report then move to IGNORE.

column1: #   Stripe sets cookies we don't control. Confirm any subenai-owned
#   cookie carries SameSite=Lax or Strict before flipping to FAIL.
#   Promotion plan: IGNORE for third-party (Stripe), but we cannot
#   express "only fail on first-party cookies" in rules.tsv. Action:
#   keep WARN; in parallel, add a unit test that asserts every cookie
#   set in functions/_middleware.ts carries SameSite=Lax — that test
#   IS the FAIL signal we want, scoped correctly.

column3: Cannot scope to first-party; covered by middleware unit test.

column1: #   Our CSP uses wildcards like `*.supabase.co`. Legitimate per-host
#   subdomain wildcards are NOT the dangerous `*` standalone. ZAP
#   doesn't distinguish; we accept this as a known-noisy rule.
#   Promotion plan: keep WARN forever. The dangerous variant (`*`
#   alone, or wildcards in script-src) is locked by
#   tests/security/headers-contract.ts — that file IS the FAIL signal.

column3: Subdomain wildcards are intentional (Supabase); keep WARN.

column1: #   The OG default image is base64-encoded in the build output (build
#   step generates it). Flag any UNEXPECTED base64 finding outside the
#   OG asset.
#   Promotion plan: keep WARN — the build pipeline embeds the OG image
#   as data-URI deliberately (saves a request on every share). Until
#   we ship a stable CDN URL for the OG asset, this is by-design noise.

column3: OG default image is intentionally base64; revisit when CDN-hosted.

column1: #   Informational — ZAP detected a modern SPA. Not a finding.

column3: Informational; subenai is a TanStack Start SPA.
